exposure: gestational age at birth (early-term, full-term, late-term, post-term)
outcome: hospital admission for lower respiratory tract infections (bronchiolitis/bronchitis, pneumonia)
cohort: A register study of 948,695 infants born in Finland between 1991 and 2008.
finding: Early-term birth was associated with an increased risk of hospital admission for lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI), while late-term and post-term births were associated with a decreased risk of bronchiolitis/bronchitis admission compared to full-term birth.
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery was associated with an increased risk of hospital admission for lower respiratory tract infections.
gest_age: 37+0 weeks and above, categorized into early-term (37+0-38+6 weeks), full-term (39+0-40+6 weeks), late-term (41+0-41+6 weeks), and post-term (>=42 weeks)
